subject: Clarify: data flow, subprocessor lineage, and cross-border handling for Lumina
messages:
From: Sophie Hart <sophie.hart@luminahealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lumina Security <security@luminahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Initial Qs — where requests are processed and which subprocessors are involved

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — helpful context. Before we proceed to an internal security review, our team needs a concise mapping of where request-level data is processed when using Redwood's hosted API and what third-party subprocessors are in the request path. Specifically: 

- Which cloud regions/locations may process the request payload (both primary and fallback regions)?
- Any subprocessors that receive request data (e.g., logging, monitoring, analytics, caching) and their countries?
- If a customer uses Dedicated or Private, how does processing locality change?
- Are there any transfers to jurisdictions of concern (China, Russia)? If so, under what conditions?

I've attached our standard questionnaire (lumina_security_q1_questionnaire.pdf) — if you can return a short mapping and any artifacts (SOC2 summary, region map) that would speed review.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Hart

Subject: Re: Initial Qs — where requests are processed and which subprocessors are involved

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi from Security & Infrastructure; he can provide the technical mapping and artifacts. High-level answers below to help your reviewers while we assemble the docs: 

- Hosted API (default): primary processing happens in the region you select for your org (us-west-2 or eu-west-1 today). Requests may be routed to a compatible region as a fallback if capacity or infra incidents occur; this behavior is governed by your org policy (we can set strict geo-only routing for enterprise customers).
- Subprocessors: the request path may touch the following categories — CDN (edge caching for streaming), observability (traces/metrics), and cloud provider infra (compute, storage). We do not send request text to third-party analytics vendors. A maintained subprocessor list (region-tagged) will be attached.
- Dedicated: Dedicated capacity pins your work to reserved GPU pools in the region you contract; cross-region fallback is disabled by default unless you enable multi-region failover.
- Private/on-prem: customer-managed — processing stays in your VPC or air-gapped infrastructure.
- Restricted jurisdictions: we do not intentionally route requests to China/Russia. Transfers only occur to regions listed in our region map and to subprocessors required for operation; we will flag any non-standard transfers.

I'm attaching a simple processing map (redwood-data-processing-map.xlsx) and Rishi will follow up with the SOC2 summary and a per-subprocessor country list.

Thanks,

Thanks for looping me in — below is a concise, technical mapping you can paste into Lumina's questionnaire. I've included explicit notes about retention and conditional cross-border movement. Happy to hop on a call if you want to walk through any rows.

On Sat, Apr 3, 2027 at 10:03 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi from Security & Infrastructure; he can provide the technical mapping and artifacts.

Summary (short):
- Ingress: API request enters via regional endpoint (customer-selected primary region: currently us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1).
- Serving: model inference runs on GPU pools in the selected region. For Hosted customers with default routing, a small percentage of requests may be served from a compatible region during capacity shaping or outages (automated fallback). For Dedicated customers, serving is pinned to the contracted region unless multi-region failover is explicitly configured.
- KV/Prefix caching: caches are regional by default; cache replication to other regions only occurs when multi-region failover is enabled.
- Logs & Observability: structured telemetry (request id, latency, status) is forwarded to our observability backend (self-hosted telemetry or cloud-managed) depending on customer tier. We do not forward raw request text to third-party analytics vendors; request text retention is controlled by the customer plan/contract.
- Subprocessors (examples, region tagged):
  * Cloud provider compute & storage (AWS us-west-2 / us-east-1 / eu-west-1) — hosts inference and ephemeral storage.
  * CDN / edge (Fastly, regional POPs) — streaming endpoints; only fragments for chunked responses are proxied.
  * Managed logging & tracing (internal ELK cluster / Datadog for some accounts) — retains structured telemetry; raw prompt text is redacted by default for hosted free-tier and kept only when explicitly enabled.
  * Backup & artifact storage (S3-compatible buckets) — used for model artifacts and retained audit logs; encryption at rest via KMS.

Conditional cross-border transfers:
- We do not route data into China or Russia for hosted inference. Transfers to other regions (including APAC) occur only if: (a) your org selects those regions, (b) you enable multi-region failover, or (c) there's an outage and you permit automatic failover in your org policy. Any such transfers are logged and surfaced in the Console audit trail.

Retention and deletion notes:
- Short-lived inference artifacts (KV cache, ephemeral model state): default retention 0–24 hours depending on model; configurable by customer.
- Request logs/metrics: default 30 days; enterprise plans offer longer retention windows.
- Deletion: we support immediate retention-zero configs and on-demand deletion requests via the Console or our support API; we provide an audit record of deletion operations.

Attached: SOC2-Audit-Summary-2026.pdf (summary), plus our per-subprocessor export as a CSV (included in the drive link).

If Lumina needs a controlled runbook (e.g., blacklisted-country hard-blocks, IP allowlists, dedicated air-gapped deployment), we can scope a Private deployment or Dedicated with strict geo-routing.

Regards,
